intro: Nebraska runs its elections county by county, through the county clerk or, in some counties, an election commissioner.

id_rule.text: Nebraska law requires a photo ID to vote, with limited exceptions. A voter who cannot get a photo ID because of a reasonable impediment, such as a disability, illness or religious objection to being photographed, can sign a Reasonable Impediment Certification. The Nebraska DMV offers a free state ID for voting.

elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Early voting in person
dates.detail: You can vote in person at your county clerk's or election commissioner's office starting 30 days before Election Day, through Monday, Nov. 2. Nebraska uses the term "early voting" for voting by mail and in person.

dates.label: Last day to register online or by mail
dates.detail: Online registration closes at midnight. A mailed form must be postmarked by this date (the third Friday before Election Day). The DMV and some state offices also stop taking registrations at the close of business.

src.label: Nebraska Secretary of State, 2026 election calendar

dates.label: Last day to register in person
dates.detail: You can register in person at your county election office until 6 pm on the second Friday before Election Day. This is also the last day (6 pm) for your county to receive an early voting ballot request to be mailed to you.

src.label: Nebraska Secretary of State, 2026 election calendar

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 8 am to 8 pm Central time (7 am to 7 pm Mountain time). An early voting ballot, by mail or in person, must be in the hands of your county clerk or election commissioner by the time polls close. Bring a photo ID.
